about: Real sound effects for cinetic films: links, never audio (the audio is fetched at film time by sfx.mjs into the film's audio/sfx/ with a licence record, and never committed). Each sound was auditioned with earshot (a forced choice between its role and cheap or cartoon alternatives: a laser zap, a video-game blip, an 8-bit sound, a cartoon effect, a comedy sound), measured: onset (first sample at 10 % of the peak), lead before it (to the first sample at 1 %), peak, loudness, floor (10th percentile of 20 ms windows), centroid, and mixed at its role's level over real music beds (a sound the bed masks in 3 of 4 tracks is refused). align: onset roles put their transient on the cue frame, peak roles (whooshes, risers, swells) their loudest point. "roles" maps a kit role to the kinds that may play it; "actions" (the actions of scripts/audio/actions.py) wins where the cast names the role's action. A sound is fetched as a WAV (file_url), from a pack's zip (archive_url + member, converted to WAV), or made of a real recording played in reverse (transform "reverse": the first transform_s seconds from its first sound, ending on its hit: the swells); "of" names the recording such a sound is made of, so a film plays it once. The ear query of a kind may be the kit's own description of the action (a tick: "a small mechanical tick, a detent clicking over"; a pop: "a bubble pop"; a card land: "a card or a sheet landing on a table"); it is stored with each sound.

mixkit-sfx.name: Mixkit
mixkit-sfx.quote: Items under the Mixkit Sound Effects Free License can be used in your commercial and non-commercial projects for free.
mixkit-sfx.limits: use inside a larger work (a film); never redistribute the file on its own, as stock, in a tool or template, or with source files; never register it with a rights-management service

kenney-cc0.name: Kenney
kenney-cc0.quote: License: (Creative Commons Zero, CC0) ... This content is free to use in personal, educational and commercial projects. Support us by crediting Kenney or www.kenney.nl (this is not mandatory)
kenney-cc0.quote_also: UI Audio and RPG Audio read: "You may use these assets in personal and commercial projects. Credit (Kenney or www.kenney.nl) would be nice but is not mandatory." The pack pages (Interface Sounds, UI Audio, Impact Sounds, RPG Audio) list "License Creative Commons CC0"; the CC0 deed reads "You can copy, modify, distribute and perform the work, even for commercial purposes, all without asking permission."
kenney-cc0.limits: none (CC0: the pack's files may be used, changed and redistributed); the zip comes from the pack page's own download button (no account, no key: a link that answers with a signed zip link, asked with the pack page as referer)

pixabay-motionstash.name: Pixabay, picked by Motionstash
pixabay-motionstash.quote: Free for use under the Pixabay Content License (each sound's own page) ... the Content for commercial or non-commercial purposes ... You do not need to credit Pixabay or the contributor of Content when you use it ... You cannot sell or distribute the Content (either in digital or physical form) on a Standalone basis. (Pixabay Terms: Content includes "Audio", which means music, sounds, sound effects and other audio representations and content.)
pixabay-motionstash.courtesy: Sound effects picked and shared by Motionstash (https://x.com/motionstashco), from Pixabay; each sound by its own creator, named in the record
pixabay-motionstash.recheck_why: pixabay.com answers scripts with a bot check (HTTP 403 on 2026-11-09), so the licence cannot be read again at film time: the record keeps the terms as read on 2026-11-09 and each sound's own page, read the same day, which named the Pixabay Content License
pixabay-motionstash.limits: use inside a larger work (a film); never sell or distribute the file on its own (no standalone distribution, so the audio is never committed: the film fetches it from Motionstash's shared folder); no sound that names or imitates a brand, a game or a device (the licence leaves trademarks and third-party rights to the user)

not_used.why: its licence allows commercial use without a credit, but pixabay.com answers scripts with a bot check (HTTP 403 on 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-09), so a film cannot search or download from Pixabay itself; the Pixabay sounds Motionstash picked and shared come from their shared folder instead (source pixabay-motionstash)
